s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive visual impairment with night blindness and scotomas
salient_findings: Inferonasal scotoma on Goldmann visual field
Abnormal electroretinogram with flat rod response
key_facts: Patient age 42
Symptoms present since childhood
Initial presentation at age 10
No symptoms except night blindness
Visual acuity 20/25 to 20/30 in both eyes
Color vision normal
Fundus examination shows few yellow spots and indistinct grayish circle
Electroretinogram shows large, slow scotopic and photopic responses
Fundus Autofluorescence shows hypofluorescence in superotemporal zones
Optical Coherence Tomography shows marked inner retinal thickening and disorganization

shortlist.label: Retinitis pigmentosa
shortlist.why_kept: Night blindness since childhood, abnormal electroretinogram, and fundus examination showing few yellow spots and indistinct grayish circle

shortlist.label: Choroideremia
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive visual impairment with night blindness, marked inner retinal thickening and disorganization on OCT, and hypofluorescence on fundus autofluorescence

shortlist.label: Leber congenital amaurosis
shortlist.why_kept: Night blindness present since childhood, abnormal electroretinogram, and severe retinal dysfunction

shortlist.label: Gyrate atrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive visual impairment with night blindness, and fundus examination showing few yellow spots and indistinct grayish circle

shortlist.label: Rod-cone dystrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Night blindness, abnormal electroretinogram, and progressive visual impairment with scotomas

raw.rationale: The patient's night blindness since childhood, normal color vision, and electroretinogram showing large, slow scotopic and photopic responses with flat rod electroretinogram are consistent with rod-cone dystrophy. The fundus examination and Optical Coherence Tomography findings also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Retinitis pigmentosa
rejected.why: While retinitis pigmentosa could explain night blindness, the lack of pigmentary degeneration in the fundus examination makes it less likely.

rejected.label: Choroideremia
rejected.why: Choroideremia typically presents with more severe visual impairment and distinct choroidal atrophy, which is not described in the vignette.

rejected.label: Leber congenital amaurosis
rejected.why: Leber congenital amaurosis typically presents with severe visual impairment from birth, which does not match the patient's relatively preserved visual acuity.

rejected.label: Gyrate atrophy
rejected.why: Gyrate atrophy typically presents with distinctive fundus findings, including sharply defined areas of chorioretinal atrophy, which are not described in the vignette.
